fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: Validation metrics including linearity (R² > 0.99), limits of detection/quantification, inter-day precision (RSD < 10%), and recovery rates (94–109%) for SCFAs in plasma, serum, feces, and mouse cecum tissue. The study compares SCFA composition ratios in human serum (92:7:1 for acetic:propionic:butyric) against previous literature and reports mouse cecum tissue concentrations, which may inform preclinical model comparisons but are not direct human tumor data.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Extract the GC-MS parameters and healthy control serum ranges for SCFAs to address the SCFA portion of the gap. Search specifically for LC-MS/MS or GC-MS protocols for inosine quantification in human serum or tumor tissue. Look for consensus guidelines or methodological papers that report SCFA or inosine concentrations specifically in cancer patient cohorts to address the cancer-specific reference range requirement.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: No protocol or reference ranges are provided for inosine quantification. The study does not cover human tumor tissue samples (only mouse cecum tissue and human biofluids). Reference ranges are limited to healthy controls; no cancer-specific reference ranges or consensus statements for cancer patients are identified. The method uses GC-MS, while the gap also inquires about LC-MS/MS parameters.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: This study provides a validated GC-MS protocol for quantifying short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in human serum and plasma, including specific analytical parameters (DB-FFAP column, SIM mode ions, temperature program), sample processing standards (acidification with HCl, MTBE liquid-liquid extraction, storage at −80 °C), and reference concentration ranges for acetic, propionic, butyric, and valeric acid in healthy human controls (e.g., serum acetic acid 4788–8823 ng/mL). The authors also detail a surrogate matrix approach using distilled water for calibration, validated for parallelism and matrix effects in serum.
